security_audit.summary: The skill is a prompt-only workflow that asks the agent to start a named Claude background agent with a handoff summary. One static external-command finding is confirmed because SKILL.md line 8 directs use of the claude CLI, while the line 10 flag reference is only option documentation.

remediation.issue: External command launch from skill instructions
remediation.suggestion: Require clear user confirmation before running claude --bg and keep the command arguments fixed. Continue redacting API keys, passwords, and personal data before passing the summary as a prompt.

content.user_title: Hand Off Work to Claude Background Agents
content.value_statement: Long sessions can lose momentum when work needs to continue elsewhere. This skill creates a concise, redacted handoff and starts a named Claude background agent.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes the current conversation for a fresh agent.
Starts a Claude background agent from the current working directory.
Uses a descriptive agent name for easier session management.
Adds suggested skills for the next agent to consider.
References existing artifacts instead of duplicating their content.
Instructs the agent to redact sensitive data from the handoff prompt.
limitations: Requires the Claude CLI and background agent support to be available.
Does not validate whether referenced files or URLs still exist.
Depends on the current agent to redact sensitive information correctly.
Does not monitor or manage the background agent after launch.

use_cases.title: Continue a Long Coding Task
use_cases.description: Pass context from a long debugging or implementation session to a fresh Claude background agent.

use_cases.title: Prepare Parallel Follow-Up Work
use_cases.description: Start a named background agent for a specific follow-up task while the current session remains available.

use_cases.title: Preserve Project Context
use_cases.description: Create a compact project handoff that points to plans, issues, commits, or design notes by path or URL.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the next agent should continue the current task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use claude-handoff to continue this work in a fresh background agent. Name the agent after the main task.

prompt_templates.title: Focused Bug Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the next agent should investigate one bug.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use claude-handoff for the login failure investigation. Include the current hypothesis, files already checked, and the next verification step.

prompt_templates.title: Implementation Follow-Up
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after planning work that another agent should implement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use claude-handoff to start implementation of the approved plan. Reference the plan file and include only unresolved decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Artifact-Aware Transfer
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when important context already exists in project artifacts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use claude-handoff for the release cleanup. Reference existing PRDs, issues, diffs, and commits by path or URL instead of copying their full content.

output_examples.input: A developer asks to continue a refactor in a fresh background session.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a short handoff with goals, current status, changed files, open questions, and suggested skills. It starts a named Claude background agent for the refactor.

output_examples.input: A team lead wants a separate agent to review a failing test path.
output_examples.output: The skill summarizes the failing test, known evidence, and next checks. It launches a background agent with a clear display name for tracking.

output_examples.input: A project has a plan document and open issue with most details already written.
output_examples.output: The skill references the plan and issue by path or URL. It avoids copying their contents and keeps the handoff focused on next actions.

best_practices: Use a short, task-specific name for each background agent.
Redact secrets and personal data before creating the handoff prompt.
Reference durable artifacts by path or URL instead of repeating long content.
anti_patterns: Do not pass API keys, passwords, tokens, or private personal data in the handoff.
Do not use vague agent names that make session management difficult.
Do not duplicate full plans, diffs, or issue text when a reference is enough.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It summarizes the current conversation and starts a named Claude background agent with that handoff.

faq.question: Does it run code from the project?
faq.answer: No. The skill itself contains prompt instructions, but it asks the agent to run the Claude CLI.

faq.question: Why does it need a descriptive name?
faq.answer: The name helps users identify the background agent in job lists, session pickers, and terminal titles.

faq.question: How should sensitive information be handled?
faq.answer: Sensitive information should be removed before the handoff summary becomes the background agent prompt.

faq.question: Can it manage the background agent later?
faq.answer: No. The user manages created agents through Claude agent management commands.

faq.question: Can Codex users use the content?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow concepts are relevant to Codex, Claude, and Claude Code handoff practices.
